1.1.label: FRS Incident Number
1.1.notes: This is a text field of 50 characters length.

1.2.label: Fire and Rescue Service
1.2.notes: This list is as defined by convergence product 3 and is a 2 character code as listed below:

1.3.label: Station
1.3.notes: This field holds the station that handled the incident. This will be a 5 character text field using the National Call Signs as defined in convergence product 3. This format is Fxx99. Prior to using the IRS each FRS will need to provide a list of station details including call signs.

1.4.label: Fire Officer ID
1.4.notes: This is an optional field which is used to record the officer responsible for completing the incident report. It is a text filed. For users of the IRS Online Forms this field will be automatically completed with details of the logged on user. Optional

1.5.label: Was this incident an 'Over the Border' Incident?
1.5.notes: Used to indicate if the incident was an 'over the border' incident

1.6.label: In which FRS was the Incident?
1.6.notes: Same list as Question 1.2 For 'Over the Border (OTB)' incidents indicates the FRS in whose territory the incident occurred. This uses the same list as Question 1.2. Note: This is defaulted to the value of Q1.2 if OTB is 'No'. The Web Service will also default the value of Q1.2 if OTN is 'Yes', but no specific value is provided via the interface. Mandatory

1.7.label: What is the other FRSs Incident Number?
1.7.notes: This is a text field of 50 characters length. This is an optional field which allows the FRS in whose territory the incident occurred to record their own incident number to allow cross-referencing.

2.1.label: What was the time and date of call?
2.1.notes: Used to indicate the time/date that the call to the incident was received.

2.2.label: What was the origin of this call?
2.2.notes: This field records where the call that raised the incident originated from.

2.3.label: What was the incident type when the call was received by the control room?
2.3.notes: This field records the incident type as received when the call was received, this could be different from the actual incident type at attendance which is recorded in Question 3.1.

2.4.label: Was this incident a 'Late Call'?
2.4.notes: Defaulted to 'No' unless Q2.3 is 'Late Fire Call'.

2.5.label: Time/Date of Stop Message
2.5.notes: Used to indicate the time/date of the incident stop message.

2.6.label: Time/Date Incident Closed
2.6.notes: Used to indicate the time/date that the incident was closed.

3.1.label: Please indicate if the incident is a Fire, Special Service, or False Alarm Incident
3.1.notes: This field records the category of the incident whether it was a 'Fire', 'SpecialService' or 'FalseAlarm'. This field is used to determine which further questions are asked.

3.2.label: What type of Property was involved?
3.2.notes: This is one of the key fields in the data collection and is recorded for all incidents. It is used to record the type of property at/in which the incident occurred. This is a large list and is defined as a hierarchy. The property types are split into the following 9 categories:

3.4.label: What was the reason for the False Alarm?

3.5.label: Please indicate if there were persons rescued, extricated, injured or killed in the incident?
3.5.notes: Used to determine further questions to ask.

3.6.label: Please indicate if there were persons evacuated in the incident with or without FRS assistance
3.6.notes: Used to determine further questions to ask.

3.7.label: How many pumping appliances attended the incident before mobilisation stopped?
3.7.notes: Used to determine further questions to ask. Determines if a fire is a primary or secondary fire.

3.8.label: Was all property (including buildings and vehicles) involved in the fire derelict?
3.8.notes: Used to determine further questions to ask. Determines if a fire is primary or secondary fire. Only shown if the Property type is one which is normally a primary fire (defined in the Property type taxonomy)

3.9.label: Was this a chimney fire?
3.9.notes: Used to determine further questions to ask. Determines if a fire is a primary or secondary fire. Only displayed if a Building fire and not derelict. Defaulted to 'Yes' if Q2.3 is 'Chimney Thatch' or 'Chimney', otherwise defaulted to 'No'.

3.10.label: Was there an attack on FRS Personnel travelling to/from or at the incident?

4.3a/b.label: Location co-ordinates (Easting and Northing)

5.1.label: Did the fire have multiple seats?

5.2.label: How long was it between Ignition and Discovery?

options.label: Over 30 minutes and up to 2 hours

5.2.notes: This field records the approximate time elapsed from the ignition of the fire to its discovery. This field together with 5.3 and the other fields relating to fire growth provide data which can be used to determine the relationship between attendance time and fire size. This is vital to accurate risk modelling and analysis.

5.3.label: How long was it between Discovery and First Call?

options.label: Over 30 minutes and up to 2 hours

5.3.notes: This field records the estimated time elapsed from discovery of the fire to the first call made to fire Command & Control.

5.5.label: Do fire safety regulations apply? (Consider if incident is not located in domestic premises).
5.5.notes: For Building Primary fires only. This field is defaulted based on the selected property type, but this allows it to be over- ridden. Also used to determine other questions to be asked.

5.6.label: Means of Escape

options.label: Exits blocked (e.g. Materials stored blocking exit)

Contents contributing to abnormal fire spread /smoke production

5.7.label: Compartmentation

Fire spread through gaps or voids in construction

6.1.label: How many officers (non-rider) attended the incident that did not travel on the FRS appliance(s)?

6.2.label: Type of FRS vehicle

options.label: L4T - 4 x 4 or other off road or specialist vehicle

6.2.notes: Knowing the type of vehicle used is key to allow IRMP and analysis of differing responses. This list is based on the FireControl Convergence Product 3 definitions but has had to be modified slightly as they have an attribute based mobilising model and the IRS records actual vehicles sent. Note: TPT = 'Prime movers / Tractor units' will not be a value that can be used for IRS system. PLT, PSF, TFF, TOC have been added for the IRS system.

6.3.label: Callsign (FRS and/or RCC callsign)
6.3.notes: This can be the FRS callsign or the RCC callsign or both. The RCC callsigns are as defined in the FiReControl convergence product 3 for mobile resources.

6.4.label: How many crew were dispatched with the vehicle?

6.5.label: Was the resource demounted from a vehicle for use at the scene (e.g. a pod)?
6.5.notes: This field is used to indicate if this was a demounted resource. For the IRS we are interested in the actual equipment not how it got there. For example a Command Unit could be a vehicle or a demountable unit. Default to No.

6.6.label: What time was the appliance mobilised?

6.7.label: What time was the appliance mobile?

6.8.label: What time did the appliance arrive at the scene?

6.9.label: What time was the appliance available for other calls?

6.10.label: Where was the Appliance Deployed from?
6.10.notes: This is used to indicate whether the appliance was deployed form the home station or not. If an appliance is deployed when 'on the run' then this needs to be known if any analysis of effectiveness of response is to be made.

6.11.label: FRS / Station ID?
6.11.notes: The value is defaulted from the FireOfficers logon username for 6.10 = HomeStation. It is only displayed for 6.10 = OtherStation . This uses the drop-down lists used for Q1.2 and Q1.3.

6.12.label: Was the Appliance Deployed from an addressable location?

6.13.label: Deployed from address
6.13.rule: At least one of Locality, Town or County is required.
6.13.notes: Address format is the same as the Q4.2 Incident Location Address.

6.14a&b.label: Deployed from co-ordinates
6.14a&b.notes: Same format as the Q4.3 Incident Location Coordinates.

6.15.label: Was any equipment used at the incident?
6.15.notes: Used to indicate if any equipment was used at the incident. For a false alarm this would normally not be required but there may be instances where resources were used, so the capability is allowed. Defaulted to Yes for Fire and Special Service, defaulted to No for False Alarms and Late Calls. For special service the user can select 'No' e.g. for Standby , or Advice only.

6.16.label: Type of Equipment Used
6.16.notes: This field records the type of actual equipment that was used at the incident. Together with Question 6.17, which records the number used, it shows what was required to handle the incident. This information can be used to allow a National analysis of response requirements and equipment usage. This will provide input to resource needs analysis and is an input to the determination of 'Best Practice'. This list is based on the FireControl Convergence Product 3 definitions but has been added to, in particular to allow for the smaller equipment items.

children.label: Railway train passenger

children.hint: Fires involving all types of roadside furniture.

children.label: Pipeline

children.label: Unidentified smell

children.label: Vehicle leaking fuel
